methodology: 6 fake jobs, each `--sleep-seconds 0.5` (the only work a fake child does), run three times with the same job set through RepositoryWorkerPool at repository_concurrency=1 (serial baseline), =2 (required default), and =3 (explicit opt-in). Measures the executor's own scheduling overhead and concurrency ceiling, NOT real repository-processing speedup -- see the caveat below.
caveat: This measures subprocess-scheduling overhead with synthetic sleeping children, not real `supervise` repository processing. It demonstrates the executor mechanism delivers the expected concurrency multiplier under ideal conditions (no shared-resource contention, no real LLM/GitHub latency). It is NOT evidence that a real portfolio run will see 1.88x/2.86x speedup, and must not be cited as such -- decision #95's own '>=1.5x speedup, <=25% coordination overhead' gate needs to be re-measured against real repository jobs before raising repository_concurrency in production. See INTEGRATION.md's required preconditions and KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md.
